Agent 13, Sharon Carter: Early pick, premium white uncommon. The C+ grades undersell it; 60.9% GIH WR with a strong +3.2 IWD and 87.7% play backs LR's B. A 3/2 clue-engine that's a must-kill and the centerpiece of WB attack-alone, but it's a goodstuff two-drop in any white deck. Much stronger on the play.
Agent Maria Hill: Solid early-pick playable, better than its B- grade suggests — 60.9% GIH with 80% play and a 3.8 ALSA means it overperforms. The teamwork-payoff text scared the guides, but it's just a fine WU/teamwork 1-drop that grows and draws; take it in white, ceiling in a real teamwork deck.
Agent of Atlas: Filler body, not a slam. 57.3% GIH WR but negative IWD (-1.8) and the high OH/play tell you it's a fine early creature whose ceiling is capped — a vanilla-ish 2/2 prowess that only shines in the aggressive RW tricks deck. Take it for that deck; pass for goodstuff.
Agent Phil Coulson: Bomb-tier, first-pick-worthy. The numbers back the hype: 66.7% GIH, 69.8% OH, +11.1 IWD and a 1.7 ALSA mean it wins from turn one, not as a synergy payoff. A 1W 2/2 vigilance anthem engine that snowballs any hero board (GW especially) and must be killed on sight.
Solid playable, better than its D+ grade and negative IWD suggest — the 56.7% GIH WR is real. Low IWD just means it does little when drawn off the top; it's a build-around 2/4 that rewards the attack-alone plan (WB) and stacks in multiples. Take it as a cheap, sticky body that holds the ground in this slow format.
Avengers Assemble!: First-pick bomb. 64.6% GIH WR, ALSA 1.6 and a 94% play rate confirm a slam — the anthem-plus-card-draw stapled together turns any go-wide white board into a runaway, and with no board wipes in the format a sticky enchantment anthem is brutally safe. LLU's A over CGB's B+ is the right read; take it.
Borough Backup: Solid playable; the 60.1% GIH WR blows past its C-/C grades, so trust the data. Two vigilance bodies plus basic-landcycling means zero drawback in a slow format: flood insurance, a splash enabler, and fuel for GW heroes/token payoffs. Take it over filler.
Brave Brawler: Solid early playable, not a slam. 59.3% GIH but a flat +0.2 IWD and 60% OH WR means it pulls its weight from turn one rather than topdecking — a fine turn-2 lifelinker that scales into a 4/3 via power-up. Guides split C-/C; take it as good filler since two-drops are scarce here.
Captain America, Super-Soldier: Bomb, first pick. 59.4% GIH at a 1.6 ALSA with 93.7% play confirms it: a 1WW first-striker that's nearly unkillable in combat and hands your hero board hexproof, dodging the format's premium spot removal. Grades (Alex A-/Mark A) match the data. Take it over almost anything.
Captain America, Wings of Freedom: First-pick bomb. 1.7 ALSA and 62.3% GIH WR confirm the LLU A-: a 3-mana flying first-striker with ward 1 that's nearly impossible to block profitably or remove cheaply, and the hero anthem pushes GW Heroes. Trust the WR over the conservative CGB B — take it over almost anything.
Captain Marvel, Earth's Protector: First-pick bomb, take it over anything. 72.8% GIH with +16 IWD and 1.3 ALSA is elite; LoL's preview "garbage" read was dead wrong (they saw a vanilla 4/5), and LLU's flash-flying-lifelink-with-indestructible-power-up bomb is what the live data confirms. Flying lifelink ambush-blocker that breaks stalls and races back.
Captain Mar-Vell, Space-Born: Solid playable, not a slam. Classic 5-mana 4/4 flyer (the format's trap tier), but flash-while-opponent-casts plus vigilance turns it into a stall-breaker and combat mind-game that earns its 56.6% GIH WR despite the D+ grade and slight negative IWD. Trust the live data over the guides' C/C-; mid-pick body.
Colleen Wing, Street Samurai: Conditional build-around, mid-pick at best. The 55.5% GIH WR is real but the negative -1.5 IWD and modest 66.8% play tell the story: she's dead weight without ~3 self-targeting spells (tricks, auras, pump). Fine in a self-target white shell, a filler 2/2 otherwise. Don't take her over generic playables.
Crowd of True Believers: Filler/sideboard. The 56.6% GIH is a mirage from a 23% play rate — only the WB attack-alone decks that can actually use it keep it in, and LoL flatly calls it an unplayable F. Don't main it unless you're committed to attack-alone; otherwise pass.
Helicarrier Strike: Solid playable removal-lite at a premium-removal scarcity. The 58.5% GIH WR and 80% play rate confirm LR's "half a notch below unconditional removal" read; deal 2 (4 with teamwork) to an attacker/blocker is exactly the efficient defensive answer WU/WB racers want. Weaker in WR/WG where you're not blocking.
Hero in Training: Premium common, take it early. 62.5% GIH on a 90% play rate with a strong 4.3 ALSA — this is a cantrip body everyone wants. A 2W 2/2 that draws unconditionally (plus 2 life with another hero) is above-rate value and a juicy connive target. Mark's B- reads truest; ignore the lukewarm C+/C grades.
Invisible Woman, Sue Storm: Trap/combo-only in normal decks — 46.8% GIH WR and a brutal -6.7 IWD confirm LLU's D- over LR's build-around hype. It's the Fantastic Four infinite-combo enabler, not a midrange card. Skip it unless you're committed to that combo shell; you'll wheel it for free.
Jennifer Walters: Top-tier mythic, take early. 65.3% GIH WR and ALSA 1.5 blow past LLU's cautious B-/CGB B — a cheap 2/3 that locks opponents out on your turn and flips into a 6/6 reach trample pinger is a two-card threat that grinds out this slow format. Trust the WR; it's a bomb.
Kree Commandos: Filler at best. The 53.3% GIH WR and negative IWD confirm the D/C-/D+ grades: a 2/1 flyer with prowess is a stat-pile that blocks nothing and dies to a breeze. Only an all-in RW/WU prowess-tempo aggro deck wants it; otherwise sideboard.
Luke Cage, Power Man: Role-player, slightly trap-flavored. 54.3% GIH with a negative -1.2 IWD and sub-52% OH WR confirms Alex's read over LR's B-: a 2/5 that only grows attacking alone is a WB attack-alone payoff, not a goodstuff card. Indestructible wrecks removal-light decks but stalls otherwise — playable, not a priority.
The Mind Stone: Solid playable, not a slam. The 58.0% GIH looks bomb-tier but it's a cheap rock that smooths your curve into the legends rather than doing the work itself — Alex/Mark's C is honest, and the flicker mode is dead with so few ETBs. Early pick for the fixing, deck-dependent payoff.
Mockingbird, Ace Agent: Trap, sideboard at best. 50.6% GIH WR with a brutal -3.5 IWD and weak 49.7% play rate vindicates the LR C-/LLU D reads: a 4-mana 2/2 that dies to any removal before the double-strike counters land. Skip unless you've got cheap protection/pump to bank the investment.
Monica Rambeau: P1P1 bomb in a sweeperless format. 64.1% GIH, +9.9 IWD, picked 1.5 — a 3-mana flyer/prowess that flips into a hexproof team-pumping engine. LLU's "bordering on busted" is right; near-unanswerable spot-removal magnet that's still hard to kill. Take it over most rares.
Murdock's Crusade: Premium removal, and the numbers blow past its D grade. 61.4% GIH WR with +4.0 IWD on a one-mana (teamwork) exile of any toughness-4+ creature — exactly the enginey midrange threats this slow format is built around. LR's sideboard read is wrong; LoL correctly moved it up. Prioritize hard in any white body-heavy deck.
Solid filler one-drop, not a true rare. The 57.2% GIH WR is decent but oh_wr is null and the C-/C+ grades and modest 55.8% play confirm he's mostly a vanilla 2/1 beater that enables teamwork bodies. Take playable removal and bombs first; fine WU/aggro early curve-filler.
Night Nurse, Healer of Heroes: Solid playable, basically auto-include in white at 91% play. Flash + lifelink + an easy two-for-one (returns any permanent, even a land) makes it a flexible value body in this grind. Trust the 59.9% GIH over the B- grade; Alex's B+ is the right read.
Okoye, Dora Milaje Leader: High pick — a top-tier white uncommon. 59.8% GIH WR with positive IWD and a 3.4 ALSA back the guides' audible UP: three bodies for four mana plus attacking first strike is premium go-wide value, and with no board wipes in this format that wide board is unusually safe. The best GW/WB go-wide payoff this color offers.
Origin of the Avengers: Solid playable, a fine early-pick floor. 57.9% GIH and a 1.9 ALSA (people take it) vindicate Mark's B over the C grade. The Saga scrys then cheats in a small hero or anthems your team — variance is real but the worst chapter still digs. Best in GW heroes.
Panther Pounce: Fringe one-of, not a slam — 55.1% GIH WR is decent but it's only played 33.8% of the time and grades poorly. It's a cantripping micro-trick that can't blow you out (you keep the clue) and turns on ETB/token synergies. Fine as a 23rd card or a single copy; don't prioritize.
Patriot, Shield Wielder: Solid white playable, not a bomb. 59.3% GIH with a near-zero IWD (+0.1) and good OH WR mark it as a curve-filler that's already pulling weight when you have it, not a card you build around. LR/LLU's "annoying but they kill it first" is fair — repeatable hexproof protection is real, but it can't save itself. Mid-pick.
Political Triumph: The best of a shaky tribe, and the numbers back it: 61.2% GIH WR with a huge 66.6% OH WR means it's an explosive turn-one play that nutter-butters in a 16-17 creature deck. Trust the WR over the D- grade, but it's a dead topdeck — only mainboard when creature-dense.
Strong synergy uncommon, sharpest in RW spells. 57.2% GIH and early 4.6 ALSA reward the deck firing noncreature spells to tap-down lands/creatures — throwback mana denial that snowballs. Guides C-/C+/B disagree; trust the WR and the live read that it dominates the RW build and combos with Super Villain Lockup.
Raft Security Officer: Better than its D+ grade — 60.0% GIH and a healthy 59.1% OH mean this pseudo-removal tapper pulls weight even in the opener, neutralizing the format's defining 4-toughness bodies. Trust the live WR over the guides' "pricey filler" read. Solid white role-player, hosts the optimistic LR take.
Red Guardian, Super-Soldier: Solid playable, a quiet premium two-for-one. 59.7% GIH WR and 86% play rate beat both the LR B and LLU C: flash 2/2 villain that ambushes an attacker or blocker for clean value. Best on defense in this grindy format, and it counts as a villain for BR. Take early-to-mid.
The Sentry, Golden Guardian: Solid playable, not the bomb its stats suggest at a glance. 55.5% GIH with flat IWD (-0.4) and OH≈GD means it doesn't generate advantage — the opponent's free 5/5 cancels yours, and ~6 commons answer it. Alex D+/Mark C- were too low; live data says fine early body, just not a windmill slam.
S.H.I.E.L.D. Spy Kit: Sneaky-good role-player. The 40.9% play rate and D grades scream filler, but a 60.6% GIH WR says it overperforms when it makes the deck — best in aggressive/attack-alone white. Cheap equipment that scries and untaps; fine tempo, never a high pick. Take late, play it situationally.
Super Villain Lockup: Premium removal, prioritize hard. ALSA 2.9 and 89.8% play say the room knows it; 57.7% GIH WR plus flash exile of a tapped creature is exactly the answer this slow format pays up for. The catch is it can't touch creatures that never attack (Mr. Fantastic), so pair with tappers like Quake. High pick.
Super-Soldier Serum: Trap rare — the D-/D grades are correct despite a passable 55.3% GIH (which leans on go-wide aggressive shells, note the null OH WR). It's a creature-investment aura in a removal-heavy slow format; you get blown out for a card. Sideboard-only, take real cards over it.
Take Up the Shield: Don't trust the D+ grade — trust the 60.1% GIH WR and +2.7 IWD, which scream premium trick. The counter sticks after combat, so it's a two-for-one in a format starved for card advantage; lifelink + indestructible blows out attacks. Alex B-/Mark C+ split resolves toward Alex. Play multiples.
Wakandan Drone Flock: Filler flyer; sideboard-to-playable depending on need. The 58.8% GIH looks fine but the 38.9% play rate and 6.8 ALSA tell the truth — it's a late table-scrap, and +0.3 IWD means it does almost nothing for you. A 4-mana 3/3 flyer with ETB scry 2; flyers break stalls, so it's a passable 23rd card, not a pick to prioritize.
Web Up: Premium removal — take it high. 61% GIH WR, 94% play rate and a 3.1 ALSA make this white's catch-all O-Ring, exiling any nonland permanent. In a removal-scarce, stall-prone format this is exactly what you want; every guide agrees. One of the best commons in the set.
White Widow, Free Agent: Flexible role-player, solid mid-pick. 57.9% GIH on a two-for-one body — counters or graveyard regrow — splits the guides (LR B+, LLU C+); the WR sits in between and says "good, not premium." The IWD is flat because you usually want it as a value play, not a topdeck. Better in plan/artifact-leaning white shells.
Aerial Doombot: Better than its split grades suggest. 57.1% GIH WR and +2.9 IWD reward an early 1/1 flyer with a late power-up mana sink — a real card in a slow air-stalled format, not just artifact-deck filler. Solid role-player; LR's C+ read beats Alex's D.
A.I.M. Scientists: Better than its D- grade suggests — a real playable. 58.3% GIH and a healthy +2.3 IWD: ETB connive smooths draws and the landcycling is real flood insurance, so it's a four-drop blue villain you actually want. The blue cycle's best member; solid in UB connive.
Atlantean Cavalry: Filler, last-table playable. 54.5% GIH with a 29.9% play rate says this is a body people only run when desperate, and the +3.7 IWD just reflects how mediocre your deck is when you draw it. A 3/2 vigilance merfolk that grows once — not an F, but never a pick you're happy about.
Atlantis Attacks: Strong stabilizer, but only ONE copy. 58.4% GIH WR with the gd_wr (60.5%) far above oh_wr (54.6%) screams late-game payoff, not an early card — exactly the WU/UG teamwork ramp finisher the guides describe. The 6/5 hexproof + double bounce is a game-ender; pitch extras to connive. Second copy is the trap.
Attuma, Atlantean Warlord: Mid playable in blue, better than its D+ grade and the guides feared. 55.1% GIH on a 3/4 that draws when merfolk attack; the body grows itself so the tiny merfolk count matters less than Alex/Mark thought. "Attack not damage" makes it a real card-advantage engine. Fine maindeck filler, not a priority.
Bold Biochemist: Decent two-drop, not exciting. The 59.0% GIH WR rides UB draw-two synergy more than raw power — a 1/3 that powers up to 2/4 and draws two is a fine relevant-late body in a slow, high-toughness format. Lean LLU's C- over Ben's 'stinks.' Playable glue in connive decks, easy cut elsewhere.
Bruce Banner: Bomb, first-pickable. 61.9% GIH WR, elite +8.2 IWD and ALSA 1.9 confirm the B grade undersells it. A 1-mana X-draw engine front that flips to an 8/8 trample/reach Hulk — but the RRGG back is hard to splash, so it's best in a deck that can support red/green. Even just the front is great.
Depower: Solid playable, the kind of cheap defensive two-for-one this grindy format rewards — a 57.6% GIH with +2.2 IWD beats the D+ grade. One mana to neutralize an attacker and replace itself; trust the data over the guides' C/C+ caution. Good blue role-player you play around.
Echo, Perceptive Prodigy: Role-player, slightly overhyped by the "you do no work" praise. The 55.6% GIH WR with negative IWD and the easy-to-forget activation (per Alex's own draft note) confirm Mark C- over LoL's gushing. A 3-mana 1/4 vigilance is a fine UB connive blocker that occasionally doubles a Killmonger ETB — take it, don't reach.
Falcon, Winged Wonder: Premium blue uncommon, draft it highly. 61.0% GIH and broad guide love (top-3 blue uncommon) — a 5-mana two-for-one of flyers that surveils on attack, exactly the stall-breaking card advantage this slow format rewards. Distributed stats dodge sweepers. Take over most commons.
Falcon's Wing Harness: Strong role-player, grab it — 59.1% GIH WR with the gap between 54% OH and 62.4% drawn confirming it's a sticky value engine, not an opener. Auto-equips for evasion plus ward, turning any ground beater into a stall-breaking flyer. Best on big bodies (UB/GU). Easily maindeck-worthy as a one-of.
Frozen in Ice: Premium common removal — prioritize it. 59.3% GIH and a healthy gd_wr (61.6%) cement this as the blue Frozen-in-Ice analogue the doctrine flags as a benchmark: it taps down, strips abilities, and locks the threat without feeding graveyard decks. Lacks flash, but in a slow stall-format clean removal is gold. Take over most creatures.
Futurist Forge: Solid card-advantage trinket; 58.6% GIH WR and +3.0 IWD say it pulls weight beyond the artifact builds the guides pigeonhole it into. ETB cantrip plus a sac-for-two later means it's never a dead draw. Take it as goodstuff filler that smooths and refuels.
Giant-Sized Flying Ant: Filler flyer that the data flatters. The 58.8% GIH paired with a 28% play rate and high 7.0 ALSA screams late synergy card, not a build-around — only the decks that need it run it. A flash flyer breaks stalls, but it's a four with no theme fit; last playable, sideboard-adjacent.
Hydraulic Helper: Build-around role-player for UR artifacts only. The 56.1% GIH is inflated by the dedicated artifact decks running it — 37.7% play means it's correctly cut everywhere else. A 2/3 mana dork that only ramps artifacts, curving into the 4-drops. Don't pick it unless you're committed to the (shallow) artifact deck.
I Am Iron Man: Role-player trick for UW tempo. 56.6% GIH WR is fine but the 41% play rate and 7.1 ALSA say it's a niche flexible card, not a staple — splits LR's D+ and LLU's C+. Making a 4/4 flyer at instant speed plus a cantrip can flat blow out combat or close games over the ground. Mid-pick filler with upside.
Iron Lad, Diverging Destiny: Role-player flyer, splashy ceiling. 55.1% GIH and flat OH/GD say it performs as a serviceable 3-mana 2/2 vigilant flyer regardless of theme; the artifact-draw engine only fires with ~15+ artifacts, which UR doesn't reliably hit (the shallowest pair — don't force it). Take as an evasive body, not a build-around.
Ironheart, Clever Champion: Disappointing rare — basically a marginal playable. Among the format's glut of 4/4 flyers it posts a weak 53.7% GIH WR, confirming the guides' D+/C- 'reads like an uncommon.' The improvise-granting upside almost never matters without an artifact shell. Early ALSA (3.4) is hype, not merit; take real cards over it.
Justice, Vance Astrovik: Best blue common-tier card, slam it. 64.9% GIH WR, +7.9 IWD, ALSA 3.0 — the live data beats the B grade and validates LLU's A-. A 3-mana 2/2 flyer that bounces an ETB and grows; it embarrasses the set's no-ETB fatties, breaks stalls, and is vicious with bounce synergy. Premium in any blue deck.
Kang the Conqueror: First-pick bomb — 1.6 ALSA and +5.7 IWD confirm it. This is the textbook Kang-tier 'no-ETB but you win if you untap' threat: a clean 4-mana 4/5 flyer (a stall-breaker by itself) with a Time Walk that ends games at 8 mana. The B+ undersells it; take it over almost anything.
Kid Loki: Build-around with a slow payoff — solid only in dedicated UB connive. The 54.1% GIH WR is unremarkable and Alex (C-) thinks it grows too slowly, against LR's optimistic B-. A 1-mana 1/1 that needs counters and second-draws to matter; fine connive enabler-adjacent, not a generic playable.
Leader, Super-Genius: Bomb, top-two rare in the set, slam it. 68.8% GIH, +15.7 IWD and 69.4% OH are elite numbers — the live data crushes the cautious C+ grade, so trust the WR. A connive-doubler that conniving every combat is a runaway engine in UB. Absolute must-kill if it's across from you.
Loki, God of Mischief: Excellent first-pickable blue rare — 1.6–2.3 ALSA, 86.5% play rate and a steady 57.7% GIH WR mark it as a premium goodstuff threat in the format's best color. The flat IWD just reflects its low pick number (it's always in your deck). Take it over almost anything; blue is #1.
Mister Fantastic, Reed Richards: Build-around trap at face value. The 53.6% GIH, negative IWD (-2.4) and 44% play rate expose it — token support is too thin, so it's usually just a 2/4 reach wall. LoL's "phenomenal" assumes a token deck that rarely materializes in draft; trust the WR. Speculative late pick only if you're swimming in repeatable token-makers.
Ms. Marvel, Kamala Khan: Build-around rare that overperforms its D grade: 56.6% GIH WR with +3.3 IWD and a 3.2 ALSA show drafters take it early and it delivers in the grind. The no-max-hand-size draw engine and hand-size body reward UB/UG card-heavy shells. Solid pick, scary enough to bait removal.
Multiversal Incursion: High-variance mythic, take it speculatively. 53.7% GIH on a 7-mana copy-your-board sorcery is unremarkable, and the F grade vs Alex's "could be A- or F" capture the swing — it does nothing without a board. But the 3.0 ALSA shows it's going early and Alex won't cut it from blue; play it, don't first-pick it.
Namor the Sub-Mariner: Powerful but work-intensive mythic; solid not premium. 56.0% GIH at a 2.5 ALSA is good, but the C-/C grades and the design's catch are real: he's a cheap flyer whose stats and tokens demand heavy merfolk/blue-pip commitment, and he gets weaker if blue is contested. Take him, but know he's a payoff, not a standalone bomb.
Pym Particles: Polarizing role-player. The oh_wr/gd_wr gap (45.6% vs 56.1%) is enormous — it's dead in your opener but great drawn into a board, which is why the guides split LR B vs LLU D. A free unblockable-attack cantrip in UW tempo; clunky elsewhere. 52.2% GIH WR says playable, not a priority.
Rewrite History: Trap / sideboard build-around. 50.5% GIH, negative IWD (-2.6), bad OH (47.5%) and a 29.5% play rate — this is LR's "F on average" plan that only pays off in a dedicated draw-two shell. The combat-tap conflict kneecaps it. Skip in goodstuff; LLU's C is generous. Leave it.
Secret Invasion: Premium removal-plus, a strong early pick. 1UU to exile a creature AND copy it with ward 2 is a two-for-one that swings games in a card-starved format; 59.7% GIH WR with +4.3 IWD and an 86% play rate. Especially nasty on cheap bodies and tokens. Take it highly in any blue deck; matches the B grade.
S.H.I.E.L.D. Deployment Drone: Premium common, every blue drafter wants it. 60.9% GIH WR and 89% play for a 3-mana flyer-plus-token two-for-one — card advantage in a format where it's scarce. Also an artifact and a teamwork body. The fact it sometimes wheels is a tell that blue/artifacts is open. Fine first pick.
S.H.I.E.L.D. Flying Car: Premium early pick — 2.4 ALSA, +4.0 IWD, 89% play back up the B grade. Evasive, recurring artifact threat that breaks board stalls in a format starved for flying; the lack of guide notes hides a quietly excellent blue rare. Take it highly.
Shuri, Wakandan Inventor: Trap-ish build-around — fade it unless you're forcing UR artifacts, the shallowest pair. 56.7% GIH WR looks ok but rides a poor 2/1 body; the copy ability is hard to exploit (Mark/Alex both land ~C). Playable as a 2-mana blocker, but the artifact synergy rarely materializes. Don't prioritize.
Stature, Size Shifter: Strong mana-sink uncommon despite the D+ grade — trust the 61.2% GIH and 62.0% OH, which blow past the grade entirely. A 1-mana unblockable-while-small body that becomes a power-up finisher and fuels teamwork tapping. The numbers say it overperforms; LR's B read is right.
Super Intelligence: Meme/sideboard trap — the 54.4% GIH WR is wildly inflated by the few synergy decks running it (49.8% play, D-/F grades). It two-for-ones YOU and feeds opposing removal; only justifiable on a hexproof body like Speedball. Don't draft it as a real card.
Super Suit: Filler equipment, late pick. 54.7% GIH but a 27% play rate and ALSA 7.2 tell the story — it's a fine free-equip combat trick that wants artifact synergies you usually won't have. No hexproof, low impact. Playable in a pinch, cuttable in most blue decks. Wheels.
Thirst for Knowledge: Trap. The 51.4% GIH WR, negative IWD and a measly 40.6% play rate confirm Alex's D — you don't want to discard your action in this grindy deck, and even fueled it's a clunky draw-two. Only the dedicated UR artifacts deck mainboards it; otherwise leave it.
Tony Stark: Premium bomb, first-pickable. The 61.7% GIH plus a monster +8.4 IWD and 2.1 ALSA tell the whole story — a 1U digger that flips to a 5/5 flying haste Iron Man cheating artifacts in. Guides B+/B undersell it; the live WR says snap it, happiest mono-blue with an artifact lean.
Trickster's Stratagem: Premium synergistic removal, especially in UB connive — grab it. 61.9% GIH and a massive +5.0 IWD blow past its C- grade; trust the data. It tucks bombs and triggers your draw-two/counter payoffs in one card. Sorcery speed barely hurts since you want it on your turn anyway. LLU's "A- if instant" and "underrated by the population" are both right.
We Say Thee Nay!: Premium blue common, take it highly. 60.3% GIH WR and +3.2 IWD back Alex's love over Mark's C+: a scalable soft counter that's brutal in this slow format where opponents tap out for their clogged four-drops. Plays well even uncast as a hard-counter threat, and feeds teamwork. A genuine pick-early clincher.
Wiccan, Rising Magician: Better than the guides' war suggests — a solid blue flyer. 56.9% GIH, +1.0 IWD; the live data sides with Ethan/Numot over Ben's "garbage." The forced flicker is awkward with no ETBs to re-buy, but as a 5-mana 4/4 evasive body with upside it overperforms its C-/D grades. Take it; great with ETB value.
The Wondrous Wasp: Bomb-adjacent — first-pick blue. The 66.0% GIH WR, +11.4 IWD, and ALSA 2.0 all scream premium: a 1U flash flyer that taps and neuters a threat is elite tempo and a stall-breaker, comfortably beating its conservative C+/B- grades. Trust the data; take it over almost anything.
Agents of HYDRA: Replaceable filler two-drop, take it mid-to-late. 52.1% GIH WR and -0.8 IWD with ALSA 6.1 mark it as a fine blocker, not a payoff — with few sac outlets the dies-into-2/1 upside is mostly cosmetic. Double-villain counts for BR villains-matter, which props it up there. Otherwise a body.
Arnim Zola, Bio-Fanatic: Replacement-level filler, and the 51.3% GIH / 47.7% OH confirm the D+ grade — this is a 2/3 whose token engine is too slow and gated to matter. Only a real BG graveyard deck wants the activation. Playable body in a pinch, never a priority.
Baron Helmut Zemo: Trap rare — pass. The 51.7% GIH WR is barely above water and OH/GD are null (small sample), and BBB on a 3/3 with atrocious stats is unplayable outside mono-black. Alex D/Mark D- is right; the connive boast doesn't redeem the mana cost. Don't let "rare" tempt you.
Baron Strucker, HYDRA Overlord: Role-player, not a build-around anchor — draft as a curve creature in BR villains, not a reason to be there. 56.1% GIH is fine but the D grade and "dodges combat / only a 3-drop if it dies" critiques temper it; a fragile 2/2 anthem that needs to untap. Fine if villains come, never a priority.
Black Widow, Super Spy: Bomb — first-pick it. 1.6 ALSA, +5.9 IWD and a 59.3% GIH WR on a mythic 1-drop that can't whiff: cheap menace that grinds card advantage in a format starved for it. Best in UB connive but goes in any black deck. One of the strongest cards you'll open.
Construct a Cosmic Cube: Below-rate rare, a fringe playable. 50.8% GIH is barely above water and the 7-counter mind-control payoff almost never lands — the recurring 2/1 menace tokens carry it, and that's a modest engine. Alex B-/Mark C split; the WR sides with Mark. Grixis/villain-leaning value, not a card to take highly off the rare slot alone.
Crossbones, Malicious Mercenary: Role-player, not a bomb. The 53.3% GIH WR matches the D+ — a 4-mana 3/3 deathtouch that needs a villain mass to snowball. The 84.3% play rate is people overvaluing the legend; it's fine in heavy BR villains but mediocre elsewhere. Mid-pick.
Cruel Alliance: Premium removal — a top black common and one of the best in this removal desert. 59.5% GIH, +6.5 IWD, exiles flexibly (anything plus 3 life with teamwork). Multiple guides call it best-in-format/best-black-common; sorcery speed barely matters given the slow play patterns. Prioritize hard.
Dark Deed: The removal benchmark — premium, pick over nearly everything but a true bomb. 59.7% GIH with a monstrous +7.2 IWD and 90.6% play; all three guides call it the best black removal, possibly the best in the format. A 1B instant that -4/-4s the 4-toughness bodies and clunky five-drops defining the set. Always take it.
Decoy Ploy: Filler, narrow BW glue. 48.9% GIH WR and -3.7 IWD confirm LLU's D+: regrowth that only matters when your deck mixes heroes AND villains, and even then it's a value-light tempo loss. Playable in dedicated BW recursion, otherwise leave it in the board.
Doctor Doom: Format-defining bomb, P1P1 over almost everything. 65.3% GIH, +11.2 IWD, picked 1.3 — makes an indestructible token army and draws every turn. Numot's "one of the better rares, not close" and LLU's "potentially the best card in the set" both check out. Worth splashing or building toward.
Doom Reigns Supreme: Synergy build-around, not a maindeck staple. The 54.4% GIH WR sits below its 82% play rate would suggest because it's 'embarrassing as a topdeck' without ~12-14 villains. Splits B-/C+ on the guides; trust the live read — only valuable when you're committed BR villains. Speculative pick, fine payoff if the deck materializes.
Elektra, Daughter of the Hand: Bomb, first-pick. 62.8% GIH WR, monster +10.0 IWD, ALSA 1.8 — exactly the premium removal-on-a-body this slow format rewards, matching LLU's A-. A 2B 3/3 with Sneak that destroys a power-3-or-less creature on ETB and can ambush. Straightforward, powerful, take it over almost anything.
Grim Reaper, Lethal Legionnaire: Below-average; "reads better than it plays" is exactly right. The 52.8% GIH masks an ugly 48.6% OH — it's clunky, must attack, and dies to the format's premium removal before the reanimation pays off. A 3/4 body floor in black, but a late playable at best.
Hour of Defeat: Premium removal — prioritize hard. The +4.9 IWD and 89% play rate confirm this is a near-auto-include: a clean 4-mana instant-speed destroy with surveil 1 upside, the kind of unconditional answer this slow format demands. Both guides rate Cruel Alliance slightly higher, but this is squarely in the take-it-early tier.
HYDRA Infiltration: Niche payoff, mostly sideboard/late. The 56.6% GIH overstates it — 24.4% play rate and 7.2 ALSA mean it only makes specific WB attack-alone grind decks, where the discard-two plus drain matters. Outside that archetype it's an unplayable do-nothing enchantment. Wheel it; take it only when committed.
HYDRA Troopers: Solid playable in any black deck, not a build-around — 52.8% GIH WR matches the walked-back hype: it can't enable itself and usually just mills 2 on turn three. You want the menace token but rarely get it on curve. Fine filler villain; don't reach, don't move into BG for it.
Kingpin's Enforcers: Niche sac-outlet, low pick. 53.0% GIH but a 44% play rate and D+ grade show it only shines in dedicated black sac/graveyard shells where a repeatable outlet matters; 3 mana to activate is too steep otherwise. The slow format forgives it slightly. Take late as a BG/sac role-player, otherwise sideboard.
Klaw, Sonic Subjugator: Premium playable. 57.5% GIH WR and +2.8 IWD validate Alex's B over the C+ floor — a cheap 2/2 with a scaling guaranteed-discard two-for-one, exactly the card advantage this format starves for. Best in BG graveyard where the yard count balloons, but good anywhere black. Take early.
Madame Masque: Premium uncommon — arguably the best in the set. 57.9% GIH and +5.2 IWD undersell a card that connives on ETB then drips 2/1 menace tokens off every second draw; the 87% play rate and 3.5 ALSA show consensus. Ben misread it, then corrected to top-2 black; the B grade and live data both say snap it in UB.
The Masters of Evil: Strong villain payoff for BR; solid but synergy-gated. The 53.3% GIH and ugly 48.2% OH reveal the catch — alone it's a fine 5/6, but the +2/+1 anthem only swings games once you've drafted villains, which is why GD (56.3%) outruns OH. A near-overrun on a developed board; the plan-tutor is flavor. Take it when you're in villains.
First-pick bomb — the +12.9 IWD is one of the highest in the set. 63.1% GIH WR and 1.6 ALSA blow past both the B grades: a 3-power evasive lifelinker with connive AND a -1/-1 anthem that quietly wrecks the opponent's whole board and over-performs vs go-wide. Slam it; great BR/UB villain payoff too.
Moonstone, Harsh Mistress: Synergy payoff, not a slam — note the split between OH (46.5%) and GD (56.5%). The low opening-hand WR confirms it's a late/connive-enabled card: dead without discard fodder, premium in UB connive once you're conniving. 53.0% overall GIH. A B-color role-player; draft it when your deck wants it, not on raw power.
Ninja of the Hand: Filler / late-pick. The 55.1% GIH WR is propped up by drawn-card synergy (low 52.6% OH WR), and a 3-mana 2/2 deathtouch with an overpriced power-up is clunky and telegraphed in this slow format. Lean Ben/Alex's low read over Mark. Playable deathtouch blocker, but don't prioritize.
Project Deathlok Soldier: Sideboard/late filler, basically a trap to maindeck. 53.4% GIH WR looks okay but the 29.9% play rate and D grades are the truth: it's a 1/2 with no villain/sac/attack-alone home that just doesn't do enough. Only consider in a dedicated graveyard-recursion shell, and even then it's marginal.
Red Room Recruit: Strong common and a key UB/BR connive enabler — likely the only sub-4-mana connive, which is scarce and prized. The 55.5% GIH plus 82% play settles the Ethan/Ben split in Ethan's favor: it smooths draws and fuels the graveyard for a buck-fifty. Prioritize in black.
Robot Domination: Build-around trap by the numbers — the B- grade is a mirage. 49.3% GIH WR with negative IWD and sub-50 OH means it underperforms unless you supply your own sac outlets (Kingpin's Enforcers, Bullseye) to trigger it on command. In a dedicated BG/BR sac shell it's strong; as a goodstuff pickup it's a liability.
Ronin, Shadow Stalker: Filler/prove-it card — pass unless you've got the vibranium equipment. 54.7% GIH with a 29.3% play rate and 6.2 ALSA confirms the D/C- grades: a narrow 2B 3/3 equipment vessel that does little on its own. A passable body in equipment-heavy black, otherwise replaceable filler.
Roxxon Brutes: Above-grade playable — 54.6% GIH WR beats Mark's D+, validating Alex's C: the basic-landcycling makes it a flexible BG card that's never dead, smooths mana early and is a 4/4 menace late. A good removal-soaker body in the slow format. Solid, unexciting midrange filler.
Stolen Stark Tech: Total filler. 55.2% GIH and a respectable +3.5 IWD look okay, but the 38% play rate and weak-trick reality (D+ grade) say it's only an enabler for black equipment/sac payoffs. Indestructible-ETB flash is cute but low-impact. Last-pick playable; don't prioritize.
Super-Skrull: Bomb-adjacent; the standout of the chunk. 60.6% GIH WR, a massive +8.8 IWD, 2.4 ALSA and 90% play rate all scream first-pick. A 3-mana 4/5 flyer that breaks stalls and unlocks an ability per splashed color — heavy-black wants this badly. Grab it and splash for the modes.
Swordsman, Sharp Scoundrel: Build-around, not maindeck-default. 55.2% GIH but a 48% play rate flags it as conditional — it needs equipment density to fire, and being legendary plus the scarcity of equipment hurts. A legit BR/equipment payoff when you've drafted the support; otherwise a 1B 2/2 filler. Speculative middle pick.
Thunderbolts Conspiracy: Trap rare — don't be seduced by the rarity. 51.9% GIH and a flat +1.8 IWD confirm the D- read despite Alex/Mark's charitable C/C-: it's a slow recursion engine wanting 13-15 villains in a format too grindy for it to matter. The body-light, turn-passing payoff rarely pays. Speculative late pick in heavy villains only.
Too Evil to Stay Dead: Trap, near-unplayable. 50.2% GIH WR with -2.6 IWD matches LLU's D-: conditional reanimation with too much setup that neither host wanted to run. The teamwork-4 unlock to hit big targets rarely comes together. Skip in favor of real cards.
Unliving Legionnaire: Filler-to-sideboard. 52.6% GIH but a bad 4-drop (3/2 flyer) and only a 35.6% play rate; both guides land near D. The 7-mana power-up bounce mode is only live in the slowest games. Playable evasion in a pinch, but you want better — take it last.
Visions of Villainy: Marginal card-draw, sideboard-ish. Effectively a 2-mana draw-two-lose-two in black villain decks, but pure card draw is rarely what this format wants (53.3% GIH WR, +0.9 IWD, weak 50.7% OH WR — a clear drawn-not-opener). Matches the D/C- grades. Last-few-cards filler when you need gas.
Whiplash, Vengeful Engineer: Niche role-player, low pick outside its deck. The 55.4% GIH WR is propped by the 57.6% oh_wr and a 50.6% play rate; enters-tapped and the equipment-count drain mean it only shines in a black equipment-aggro/villains build. Play it if you care about villains, otherwise pass for cleaner bodies.
Widow's Bite: Solid removal-ish playable — cheap instant-speed -2/-2 is genuinely useful against this format's small and menace creatures, and removal is at a premium. The 55.8% GIH backs the C grade; teamwork-3 deathtouch upgrade is gravy you rarely pay. Reliable black role-player, take over filler.
Yellowjacket, Heartless Marauder: Solid two-drop — a premium-ish flyer in a format starved for them. 57.0% GIH WR and +4.9 IWD with an 85% play rate show it pulls weight even without forcing villains; it plays as a 2/2 flying lifelink on offense, and flyers break the stalls this format produces. Best in BR/WB villains, weak on defense.
Avengers Disassembled: The format's only pseudo-wipe, and a premium pickup in UR/GR — but read the room. 55.6% GIH and 3.1 ALSA undersell it because so many bodies have 4 toughness; the deal-3-to-all mode plus Stone Rain shines as removal in spell decks. Trust the C+ over the D+ grade; archetype-dependent but high-ceiling.
Blazing Crescendo: Marginal trick — 50.3% GIH WR and negative IWD put it at the bottom of red's playables despite being its premium combat trick. Cantripping pump that targets your own creature and turns on attack-alone payoffs (Iron Fist), so it's deck-dependent. A single copy at most in RW spells; otherwise pass.
Crimson Operative: Best-in-class red common — prioritize. 54.8% GIH undersells it; this is a genuine two-for-one (3/2 prowess artifact villain that impulse-draws) in a format starved for card advantage, and it wheels hard so you can table multiples. Numot's warning holds: it's a value body, not a finisher, and weaker without removal backing it. Strong early-mid pick.
Death to Our Enemies: Trap. The ugly 46.4% GIH WR and -4.6 IWD bury the build-around B hype — plans are topdeck-dead and this one wants a noncreature-heavy red deck the format doesn't support. Only on-curve turn-two is it real. Pass; sideboard material at best.
Evil's Thrall: Trap / sideboard. The 50.9% GIH and rock-bottom 20% play rate are damning — Threaten effects need sacrifice outlets, which barely exist here, so you just hand the creature back. Guides C+/C-/D+ are charitable; treat as a niche tempo play in a villain-sac shell, otherwise leave it.
Fin Fang Foom: Well-statted top-end, fine not great. 53.3% GIH with a +0.0 IWD says the 3/5 flyer body is doing the carrying, not the spell-copy ability — Mark's "rarely matters" beats Numot's engine dreams in practice. As a cheap evasive villain it breaks stalls and fills your curve top. Mid-pick; don't draft your deck around the copy text.
Hawkeye, Master Marksman: Premium rare, take early. 59.1% GIH WR and a strong +6.8 IWD support the LLU B+ over the cautious CGB B-: a 2-mana first-strike/reach body with a repeatable trick-arrow menu that grinds value, picks off players, and loots. Flexible and efficient enough to anchor any red deck. Could be A-tier.
Hawkeye, Young Avenger: Build-around, fragile and weak standalone. 54.1% GIH masks a legend that dies to the format's premium removal and does nothing without burn to redirect. Ethan loves it as an RW/burn engine (Lightning Strike, Truck Toss go face); LLU's D is the standalone read. Speculative pick only if you're in the spells deck.
Hawkeye's Bow: Trap / near-unplayable. 23.3% play rate tells the story — only the (nonexistent) equipment deck wants a +1/+0 reach equipper with no toughness boost. The 54.6% GIH WR is a tiny, self-selected sample. Matches the D- grade; leave it in the pack.
Hex Magic: Trap, leave it in the binder. No GIH WR, 12.1% play, ALSA 7.4 and an F grade — the data sides with Mark's D over Alex's C. A 3-mana impulse-draw that's awkward whenever you're holding a bomb and great only with a balanced hand. Too narrow and inefficient for this grindy format; don't main it.
Hire a Crew: Trap/sideboard — the 45.7% GIH and -2.5 IWD are damning, and the 11% play rate means even drafters who first-pick it cut it. Ben's "every box it checks is too small" wins decisively over the data. Each mode is too weak; don't play it.
HULK SMASH!: Role-player removal, not premium — only your last few removal slots. 56.1% GIH WR is decent but the awkward modal fight/destroy-artifact sizing earns Alex's "more constructed than Limited" knock. Take it when you're short on real removal and have deathtouch/prowess to abuse it; otherwise it's a filler trick.
Human Torch, Johnny Storm: Mediocre playable, RG/RW only. The -1.2 IWD and 48.9% OH are red flags — it's worse in your opening hand than drawn, a synergy/ping card not a standalone threat. Plays as a 3/2 flyer in damage; the 52.8% GIH is propped by good decks. A role-player, not a high pick.
HYDRA Assault Robot: Solid filler with upside — 53.1% GIH WR, even across OH/drawn, makes it a reliable 1/3 body that pings when villains/artifacts enter. Wants UR/BR for the trigger density; weak in GR. Good early-defensive playable that stacks chip damage in the right deck. Mid-pick.
Iron Fist, Living Weapon: Build-around with a target on its back — pass unless committed. Sub-50% GIH (49.7%) and negative IWD confirm it's fragile and synergy-gated; LoL's "best red card" only applies in a dedicated RW spell-target shell. The doctrine flags it as exactly the cheap linchpin opponents snipe turn three. Low pick as a payoff, premium target for your own removal.
Jessica Jones, Private Eye: Solid value engine. 58.9% GIH WR and +4.3 IWD clear the C- grade comfortably — a slow Mulldrifter that draws repeatedly if she sticks and refunds when killed, exactly what the grind rewards. Understatted with no evasion, so she wants a stabilized board; good mid-pick, best in RW.
K'un-Lun Warrior: Filler two-drop you play when curve demands. 53% GIH, slightly negative IWD, late 7.0 ALSA — a passable 2/2 looter that's awkward (sacs an artifact you may not have) and notably not a villain. Guides D/C; you can't be picky on twos here, so it makes RW decks as a body, nothing more.
Kree Sentinel: Replaceable common, low pick. 53.9% GIH with a flat +0.2 IWD means the 5/5 reach body is barely above a bye — it ticks villain/artifact boxes and walls flyers, but Alex calls it the worst of the bunch. Playable filler in BR villains or UR artifacts; take it late when you need bodies, not earlier.
Lightning Strike: Premium removal — the benchmark burn, prioritize it. 56.2% GIH WR, 3.2 ALSA and 90% play rate vindicate LR's B over the LoL/LLU "deal 3 misses 4-toughness" hot take: removal is scarce and at a premium in this slow format, and red is the best splash. Always playable, take it high.
Loki Laufeyson: Solid playable with pop-off upside, undervalued by its C- grade. 52.4% GIH on a cheap 2/1 that copies your burn/removal once you untap — doubling a Lightning Strike wins games. Fragile and setup-dependent (LR's B-/fragile caveat), but the cheap red enabler is exactly what spell decks want. Take it mid-pack.
Machinesmith Automaton: Filler at best, build-around bust. 52.1% GIH WR and a D- grade confirm it: a 2/2 that grows per artifact can't hit enough triggers since the UR artifact lane is the format's shallowest. LR's C+ assumes a deck that rarely comes together. Don't force it; replaceable body.
Misty Knight, Hero for Hire: Marginal playable, mid-pick. The 54.2% GIH WR and -2.1 IWD undercut the C+ grades; she's good early stats (the only 3-power two-drop, nice for teamwork) plus a late rummager, but red holds her back per LoL. Take her as a curve-filler, not a priority. Better with connive/cyclers to discard.
Mjölnir, Hammer of Thor: First-pick bomb, full stop — 1.5 ALSA, +8.8 IWD, 61.7% GIH. The A-/A grades are right and the B undersells it. It's split removal that's "basically always playable": 4 damage on ETB plus a repeatable board-damage mode, even without a worthy carrier. Take it over nearly everything.
Photon Blast Barrage: Niche playable with a high ceiling in the right shell. The 57.1% GIH WR masks a big OH/GD split (51.7 vs 60.8) — it's clunky in your opener but a token-mopping blowout drawn later. Bad into high toughness; great vs go-wide, and a near-combo with Red Hulk in RG/RW. Sideboard-flex maindeck, not a high pick.
Quicksilver, Brash Blur: Marginal, near-cut. 50.4% GIH is essentially a coin-flip and +0.1 IWD means drawing it changes nothing; the 49.0% play rate and D grade say the field agrees. No notes to redeem it — provisional read is a fringe playable you bench when better reds show up. Don't prioritize.
Red Hulk: Polarizing midrange threat — the 53% GIH WR splits the difference between its A-or-D ceiling: a 6/7 reach-trample enrage that crushes red/green removal but dies to bounce. Combos with Photon Blast Barrage for near-lethal. Take it as a strong standalone beater in RG/RB; just know it's matchup-dependent.
Repulsor Blast: Playable red removal, slightly below rate. 52.5% GIH on 4-mana-deal-5 — the doctrine wants red to kill bigger things, and this does, with the teamwork face-damage saving it from being overcosted. 77% play rate means it makes most red decks. Solid-but-unexciting; take it when you need removal, which is often.
The Scarlet Witch: Provisional, grade-based read: no WR data and a 26.7% play rate signal drafters correctly leave it. The D+ is right — there aren't enough 4+-MV instants/sorceries in MSH to make the cost-reducer matter. Build-around-only curiosity; pass in goodstuff.
Speed, Young Avenger: Trap-leaning role-player. The split is stark: 56.5% OH WR but 49.8% drawn and -3.5 IWD mean it's only good in your opener as early aggro and dead later — a 2/2 haste that folds to evasion and isn't a villain. Trust the negative IWD over the C/C+ grades; fringe RW aggro filler.
Stark Industries Executive: Niche ramp one-drop, role-player. 52.8% GIH but a telling 48.7% play rate — most decks cut it because clunky Treasure-making asks too much for too little. Real home is UR Iron Man / artifact splashes where the turn-two ramp and Treasures matter. Otherwise a marginal body; pick it for the synergy deck or pass.
Super Speed: Sideboard / near-unplayable. 50.3% GIH WR with a dismal 9.1% play rate and 8.1 ALSA tells the real story — almost nobody runs it. A flash haste-aura trick with no home (LLU C-/D+); the haste can occasionally steal a game, but it's two-for-one bait. Pass.
Team Tactics: Finisher/trick, situational. 50.5% GIH and negative IWD (-2.8) show it's a do-nothing in your opener that wins out of nowhere off teamwork double-strike. Best in RW go-wide, nasty with deathtouch, but doesn't protect your creature. A C-grade combat trick — sideboard-flexible role-player, not a high pick.
Thor, God of Thunder: Bomb — first-pick, splash-worthy. The mythic numbers are absurd: 62.4% GIH WR, +12.9 IWD, ALSA 1.4. A 5/5 flyer that recurs your best instant/sorcery/equipment and pings on every noncreature spell is a giant Snapcaster that breaks stalls and grinds value. A grade, A play. Take it every time.
Truck Toss: Solid removal, prioritize but not premium. 53.4% GIH WR with a slightly negative IWD reconciles the guide split — it's playable burn, not a slam; LLU's C- beats LoL/LR's B. Four damage to any target is the magic number and kills most things, just a touch expensive at 2RR. Good in any red deck, especially with vehicles.
Vision of Love: Filler/sideboard — a 50.3% GIH and 25% play rate confirm the D grade. Card-draw that costs you a card or artifact is a bad rate in a format where you'd rather just play a creature. LR's optimism is misplaced; skip unless you're desperate for noncreature spell count.
Volcanic Villain: Trap/filler — basically don't play it. The 47.7% GIH WR, 7.6 ALSA and 17.7% play rate are damning: a vanilla 3/2 haste power-up with no ETB, exactly the kind of body that gets outclassed. Alex D-/Mark D is correct. There's always a better card; this is a 24th-card at best.
Wonder Man, Hollywood Hero: Trap-flavored 5-mana 4/4 flyer — the classic "big dummy" with a payoff that rarely fires. 52.5% GIH and +0.3 IWD confirm the D+/C grades: a body that gets raced in a slow format, with a power-up-doubler ability you seldom activate twice. Last-pickable; better 5-drops exist.
Ant-Man's Army: Premium common, prioritize it — 57.7% GIH WR understates how good the glue is. A 3-mana 3/2 making Food or Treasure does fixing, ramp, splash-enabling, artifact-count and lifegain in one card; Numot ran four. The format's best soup/fixing common. Snap it up, especially if splashing red.
Call Damage Control: Sideboard filler, near-unplayable. 50.3% GIH with a bad -3.0 IWD and an 18% play rate — narrow, low-impact regrowth that's strictly worse than the black equivalent. Doesn't affect the board the turn you cast it. Skip in nearly every deck.
Claim the Kingdom: Filler-to-trap. The 51.6% GIH WR and negative IWD match Alex's D+/Mark's D- — a landfall plan that clogs your own curve and folds to the format's exile/sac removal. Both reviewers' least-favorite plan. Don't main it unless desperate for a green non-creature.
Doc Samson, Super Psychiatrist: Below-rate ramp you don't want. 53.5% GIH and a flat +0.3 IWD confirm both guides' D+: a 5-mana 3/6 (or 6/3) Doubling-Season dork that adds little even in the counters decks it's supposed to enable. The 5-drop slot wants a threat, not this. Last-cut filler for RG/GU.
Earth's Mightiest Heroes: Boom-or-bust teamwork payoff for WU/GW — only pick it if you're committed to a body-heavy build. 58.4% GIH reflects the games where teamwork-5 is online and it dumps a board; off-theme it's the "slightly bad" half Mark warns about, hence the D- floor. Mark's B- over Alex's C- is the right read in a built teamwork deck.
Epic Fight: Solid rare, slightly underrated. 57.0% GIH WR and 2.3 ALSA back Mark's B+ over Alex's B-: doubling P/T plus a fight is both removal and a race-ender in one card, which is exactly what a grindy green midrange deck wants. Take it as an early-ish playable, not quite a bomb.
Giant Growth: Sideboard trick in this slow format. 55.6% GIH is real but driven by GD (58.4%) over OH (51.5%) — it's a blowout-when-drawn-live card, dead in your opener, and only 29.0% play rate. LLU's D- is harsh but the bar is conditional +4 now. Keep one or two for the board; rarely maindeck.
Go Nuts!: Premium green interaction, high pick. One-mana fight (teamwork 3) plus a counter is hugely tempo-positive — 58.5% GIH WR and an 84% play rate back the hosts' 'has been nuts.' Cheap removal is gold in a format short on it. Remember you need 3 power already on board to pay teamwork. Prioritize in any green creature deck.
Guerrilla Gorilla: Replaceable filler with sideboard value. 56.3% GIH WR is fine but the 54.4% play and D+/C- grades say it's a body first; the real draw is being one of few answers to Plan enchantments and artifacts, which makes it a best-of-three card. Maindeck a 2/2 reach as needed, board it in when relevant.
Hellcat, Undying Vigilante: Garbage as a maindeck pick despite a 57.2% GIH inflated by heavy-green decks that can cast GG on time — note the C grade and Alex's D+. Never warp toward it; it's a reward only in near-mono green, where it's also fine Killmonger sac fodder. Otherwise pass.
Hercules, Prince of Power: Solid midrange role-player. 54.6% GIH WR with a slightly negative IWD (it's a curve-filler, not a bomb), but the power-up to a 4/4 vigilance/indestructible/haste gives a real threat-of-activation that's hard to block at five mana. Good RG/GW body; take it as a creature, don't overrate the level-up.
Heroic Feast: Trap build-around, essentially a sideboard card. The 57.0% GIH is a mirage off a 53.8% play rate — lifegain is unsupported in this set, so this is a once-a-format pet deck (D-/D+ grades agree). Pass it for any real playable; provisional read leans hard on the grade.
Hulkling, Burgeoning Bruiser: Replaceable filler unless you're in counters — 53.4% GIH WR and roughly zero IWD say it's "just stats" alone, exactly Alex's read over Mark's. Likely a 3/4 vigilance on turn four. In a dedicated +1/+1 / evolve home it becomes a counter-engine, but the GU pair is weak. Mid-pick body.
Ka-Zar of the Savage Land: Bomb-uncommon — snap pick, take over Serra Angel per Alex. 60.7% GIH, ALSA 2.8 and the highest common/uncommon grade in the set: a play-lands-off-the-top engine plus a growing Zabu cat is overwhelming card advantage that takes over long games. Both bodies must be answered. As high a green pick as exists outside rares.
Knight of Wundagore: Filler. The 53.9% GIH WR and -1.0 IWD land it between the D and C- reads — a replaceable 2/1 trample that only matters if you've stacked counter sources and the fight spell. Fine as a curve-filler in RG/GU power-up; otherwise a 23rd card.
Mister Hyde, Monster Within: Trust the live WR over LR's optimism — a fine playable, not a B-. 54.9% GIH and a flat +0.5 IWD: the upkeep draw/grow engine is slow and the unchecked reward modest, so it's a 3-mana must-answer body rather than a bomb. Reconcile LR's B-/LLU's D+ to a solid-but-unexciting green two-drop villain.
Mole Man, Moloid Master: Underwhelming rare; modest pick. The 56.1% GIH overstates a 1/1 whose graveyard-land engine has almost no enablement in this set — Alex D+/Mark D nail it. Token-on-landfall is slow value in a slow format. Playable green legend, but you're picking the name, not the impact. Take real cards over it.
Pet Avengers: Solid playable but ceiling-capped. 57.8% GIH WR with the gd_wr (59.3%) over oh_wr (55.6%) flags it as a board-stall soaker, not a stall-breaker — both guides warned it "makes the board stall rather than break it." A fine 4/4 reach with a power-up mana sink for green decks that want to grind; not a reason to go green.
Powerful Broker: Filler. 52.5% GIH but negative IWD (-2.4) and a 27.3% play rate — the localized proliferate is a late-game-only, counters-deck ability with no payoff in goodstuff. Stats are a fine 3/3 villain body; that's all you're getting. Last-pick deck-rounding, nothing more.
Punishing Punch: Premium removal — a top green pick, take it early. 60.1% GIH WR, +5.0 IWD, ALSA 3.3 confirm the LoL/LR 'best green removal' read: a near-catch-all instant that's often one mana in BG graveyard. Numot took it over a red/gold card P1P2. Trust the data over LLU's modest C+; grab it hard.
Rapid Rescue: Late-pick filler with a real disagreement attached. The 56.7% GIH WR is inflated by selection — note the 20.4% play rate; it's only good in a high-permanent-count green-black shell (smooths into HYDRA Troopers) and Ben famously soured on it live. Never want the second copy. Take it last, deck-dependent.
Reptil, Dinomorpher: Trap — the 54.7% GIH hides a +0.3 IWD and 38% play rate, and a one-turn stat boost for that much mana is, per LR, "a way to lose games." Greater-or-garbage: garbage. The grades (D / D+) are right; leave it for someone else.
Restorative Technique: Filler — only if you have genuine splash demand. 52.2% GIH WR, 37% play rate and a near-zero IWD confirm Alex/Mark D: it's a worse Rampant Growth with no board impact, and fixing in this good-mana format isn't worth a card. Late playable for a counters/ramp GU build, otherwise cut.
Rick Jones, Destined Sidekick: Niche, mostly cut — provisional with no WR-vs-field signal beyond a brutal 17.6% play rate. A G 0/3 that blocks and digs for heroes/enchantments but decks you fast; wants ~10 heroes to justify. The 57.1% GIH is small-sample synergy noise. Dedicated GW heroes only, otherwise filler.
Savage Land Dinosaur: Fine playable, lean BG — 54.9% GIH WR for a 7/6 trampler that landcycles when you don't want it is exactly the cycler story: never dead, hits land drops, feeds the graveyard count. Single green pip makes it slightly better in BG. Solid curve-topper, unexciting. Take when you need top-end.
Serpent Specialist: Solid green common, mid-pick. 56.1% GIH on a deathtouch power-up body — threat-of-activation on a deathtoucher means it trades up and blanks attackers all game, which is exactly what this grindy format rewards. "Could see C+" is right; a quietly above-rate playable that makes most green decks.
Shang-Chi, Master of Kung Fu: Good early pick despite the modest 54.9% GIH WR; the 2.3 ALSA and 80% play rate show it's taken and run highly. A 2-mana hero granting haste and restricted ramp that opponents must respect, especially alongside power-up payoffs. Alex's B- over Mark's C+ — synergy-leaning but a real enabler in RG/GU.
She-Hulk, Jade Defender: Top green pickup, prioritize. 61.1% GIH, +5.4 IWD, an above-rate 4/4 reach trample that doubles as removal — read the power-up as a split card (4/4 body or 2-mana destroy an artifact/enchantment the turn it lands, hitting plans/equipment/artifact creatures). Live draft confirmed "could've run two"; take it over its C grade.
Super Strength: Trap aura — leave it. 8.0% play rate is the whole story: nobody runs the +4/+4 trample-ward aura because the no-flash, card-disadvantage two-for-one risk is brutal even if it occasionally kills out of nowhere. The 51.9% GIH comes from a tiny optimistic sample. Sideboard at best.
The Thing, Ben Grimm: Big-dummy trap. 54.8% GIH WR with a flat +0.2 IWD undercuts the size: LR nailed it as "absurdly large, not absurdly good" — a 6-mana 7/7 with no ETB and no self-protection that gets removed or chumped while you fall behind. Marginal in heavy GW Heroes; otherwise a passable late playable, nothing more.
Tigra, Feline Fury: Off-theme build-around, marginal. 55.1% GIH but the high OH (57.6%) over GD (53.3%) suggests it's pulling weight as an early flash-trample body, not the lifegain engine it wants — the set lacks ~6-7 triggers to feed it. A 1G flash creature is fine; the "please gain life" text is a trap. Playable, not a priority.
Training Regimen: Marginal role-player, mild trap. The negative -0.8 IWD and 52.9% GIH WR expose a bodiless enchantment that 'does too little' — it only matters once you're already making creatures with trample/counters. LR's D over LLU's C-. Snowballs in a long game, but it's the first cut from a real green deck.
The Unbeatable Squirrel Girl: Bomb, first-pick. 61.3% GIH WR, +7.0 IWD, ALSA 2.1 — the live data backs the B+ grade. A GGG 4/4 that's immediately 5+ stats and snowballs tokens if it untaps; classic must-kill that runs away with the game. The triple-green cost ties you to green, but it's worth building around.
Undercover Skrull: Excellent common and an underrated early pick — 59.5% GIH, 62.4% OH, 88% play all beat the C grade. Two-mana any-color fixing that ramps 2-into-4 and grows into a 3/3 all-types body with a graveyard; rare praise for a green manalith. Take it high in any green deck.
Wakandan Royal Guard: Fringe playable — a removal-soaker, not an exciting common. 55.4% GIH WR with flat IWD says it's fine but replaceable; a 5-mana 4/4 vigilance with a small counter ETB is a midrange body that earns a touch more in GW heroes (target a hero for +2). Ben's "out of place" read is closer than Ethan's bump — a 23rd-24th card.
White Tiger, Ava Ayala: Premium green uncommon, take it early. 58.2% GIH on an 89.4% play rate and 3.7 ALSA — a sticky 2-drop that stays relevant by powering up into a counter plus a 4/4 Tiger God late. Best green common-slot creature per all guides (B). A genuine first-few-picks green card.
World War Hulk: Overrated rare, just an overrun — 53.2% GIH WR and flat IWD confirm Alex's C-/Mark's D+: a saga that ramps then doubles/tramples for the kill, but premium overruns are rarely what this slow format needs and it has lots of ifs. Playable in RG go-wide, but don't take it over real removal or threats.
Abomination, Terrifying Titan: Strong Gruul payoff, take early in RG. 56.9% GIH and ALSA 3.6 back the B grade — a 4/4 trample that powers up to fight is a sticky two-for-one and a real threat, with the fight mode doubling as removal. Wants the power-up/ramp shell to fund it, but good enough to first-pick into Gruul.
Absorbing Man: Bomb. 61.3% GIH WR, +5.9 IWD and a stellar 63.4% OH WR — it wins from the opening hand, no synergy required. The B- grade undersells it; this UG villain is a first-pick that warps your draft toward blue-green. Take it over almost anything.
Alien Invasion: Solid rare, but the data cools the B grade. 52% GIH and a near-flat 51.4% drawn WR despite a very early 2.6 ALSA — drafters reach for it more than it pays off. A go-wide RG enchantment that's fine in its lane (go-wide is safe with no wipes), but it's a build-toward, not a slam; trust the modest WR.
Ant-Man, Colony Commander: The GU counters signpost, and a lukewarm one. 52.6% GIH with a negative -2.6 IWD is damning — drawing it actively correlates with worse games, echoing both hosts' "asks for a lot of mana and work for a minor payoff." GU is the weakest pair anyway. Fine if you're forced into it; never a reason to be in it.
Ares, God of War: Solid gold playable, mid-pick. 56.5% GIH WR and +6.1 IWD with no guide notes — the data carries it: a BR Villains body that meaningfully improves your deck when drawn. Lean into it if you're in the BR villains lane; the CGB B- looks right. Take it when you're committed to the colors.
Armor Wars: Provisional skip — read is grade-based with no WR splits available. 50.4% GIH and -0.0 IWD on a C- saga is replacement-level, and UR artifacts is the shallowest pair you shouldn't force. The 49.5% play rate says even drafters who took it often benched it. Speculative at best; leave it unless deeply in artifacts.
The Astonishing Ant-Man: Solid GU signpost, better as an opener. Note the 60.3% OH WR clears its 57.7% GIH WR and +4.3 IWD — it wants to land early and snowball, fitting the +1/+1 counters pair the doctrine ranks weakest. With no guide notes, lean the data: a fine midrange playable, not a bomb. Mid pick if you're in blue-green.
Avengers: Under Siege: Bomb, first-pick despite empty notes. 63.0% GIH WR with a massive +11.4 IWD and ALSA 2.4 — those are top-of-set numbers. A BR saga that grinds out enormous card and board advantage, exactly the two-for-one engine this slow grindy format craves. The signpost-tier payoff for BR villains; take it very high.
Beast, Erudite Aerialist: Below-average gold uncommon — the 51.2% GIH and -1.0 IWD confirm both guides' lukewarm read. It's a 4-mana 3/3 doing a lot of work for a small payoff, and conditional flying isn't reliable stall-breaking. Playable in GU counters but never a reason to be there; low priority.
Black Panther, Vanguard: Strong GW signpost — high pick if you're in the pair. 58.0% GIH WR and a 3.9 ALSA confirm Numot's respect for it as a real heroes-go-wide payoff that can pump a team and close fast. GW heroes-matter is the #2 archetype and low-effort; this is its engine. Slam it when GW, irrelevant elsewhere.
Black Widow, Double Agent: Strong in its lane, solid otherwise. The 57.1% drawn WR and "effectively unblockable attacking alone" make her oppressive in WB attack-alone, and counting as both Hero and Villain is real upside. 55.6% GIH is good for a gold uncommon; the C- grade is too low. Prioritize in WB, fine splash elsewhere.
Bullseye, Death Dealer: Good gold uncommon, take it when in BR — 53.7% GIH WR, 3.8 ALSA and 80% play rate make it a reliable villains-matter playable in an auto-on archetype. Not a bomb but a clean, efficient threat that anchors BR. Solid early-mid pick if you're in the colors.
Captain America, Living Legend: Premium WU uncommon — high pick. 60.2% GIH on a 3/4 vigilance that untaps your team enables teamwork-then-attack and turns the Helicarrier into a free crew-and-swing. Well-statted enough to be good even outside a dedicated teamwork build. The signpost the WU deck wants; take it early.
Cloak and Dagger, Entwined: Premier bomb of the chunk. 62.4% GIH WR, a monster +8.5 IWD, 2.7 ALSA and B grade all align — this WB hero just wins games. No reconciliation needed; the data and grade agree. First-pick it and commit to white-black.
The Coming of Galactus: Bomb — first-pick, splash for it. 63.6% GIH, an enormous +11.6 IWD, and a 1.6 ALSA make this BG saga one of the best cards in the set; the A- grade is fully earned by the live data. Take it over almost anything and build to cast it.
Daredevil, Man Without Fear: Premium RW gold rare — high pick whenever you're near those colors. 61.1% GIH, +5.3 IWD, and a strong 57.8% OH (so it's good even early, not just as synergy glue) all beat the B- grade. Trust the data: this is a top-tier threat for the spells/aggro pair. Take it early.
Ghost, Spectral Saboteur: Role-player, synergy-dependent. 53.0% GIH WR with +3.1 IWD but only 49% play rate (CGB D+) — a UB connive piece that's fine in its lane and underwhelms outside it. Take it as a mid playable when you're already in UB; not a card to splash for.
Hulk, Gamma Goliath: Premium Gruul beater, take it highly in RG. 55.1% GIH with positive IWD (+2.2) and the kind of GD-over-OH (57.5 vs 51.6) you'd expect from a top-end threat that wins the late game. A 5-mana 6/5 reach-trample that punishes non-answers by going 9/8. B grade is right; the headliner of the power-up deck.
Iron Man, Master of Machines: Conditional signpost — only when you're already in UR artifacts. The 55.6% GIH WR is unremarkable and the deck is the format's shallowest; LoL/Numot both repeatedly passed it ('blue-red otter'). Strong engine if uncontested, dead if removed. Don't first-pick it to force the lane; take it as a signal, not a commitment.
Kang, Temporal Tyrant: The UB connive signpost and a solid pick, but no slam — 55.4% GIH with a healthy +4.5 IWD says it grinds value rather than dominates, the "understated signpost" LoL describes. A 4-mana 3/4 that connives on attack and drains on your second draw; great glue for UB draw-two, just don't first-pick it over real bombs or removal.
Killmonger, Scourge of Wakanda: Premium pick and the best gold uncommon in the set — 62.3% GIH and a massive +8.7 IWD confirm LoL's "two gradations ahead" call. It's removal plus a body plus a yard-enabler, the BG graveyard linchpin and a genuine splash card. Worth pivoting into black-green for; take it nearly P1P1.
King T'Challa: Bomb — first-pick caliber. The 64.2% GIH WR, +7.6 IWD and 1.6 ALSA (nearly always taken P1) are elite; the B grade undersells it badly, so trust the WR. A WU mythic that the field already snaps up; if you see it, take it and let it pull you into white-blue.
The Kingpin of Crime: Solid-to-strong WB rare, draft it. 55.7% GIH and a 57.4% drawn WR back the B grade, and a 3.6 ALSA means it's contested. No guide notes, but the live data says a real threat that pulls ahead — a high pick whenever you're in white-black. Take over most commons.
Madame Hydra: Trap — the worst card here. 48.7% GIH WR (below 50%) confirms LoL's "terrible": a 4-mana 2/3 do-nothing that needs you to cast villains to do anything. It's literally why BR underperforms. Don't play it; it's a sideboard card at best.
The Mighty Thor, Jane Foster: Bomb rare, first-pick. 63.7% GIH, ALSA 2.4, 64% OH WR — every number screams slam, and a flyer of this caliber breaks the board stalls this slow format produces. No guide notes needed; the data is unambiguous. Take it over almost anything.
Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur: Strong on paper but a synergy trap in practice. The 56.3% GIH WR with a flat 0.0 IWD tells the story: needs artifact density AND second-card draw, which most pools lack — Numot found Echo simply better in the same UG shell. B grade is the ceiling, not the floor. Take it only if your UG artifacts deck is already humming.
The Ruinous Wrecking Crew: Bomb-tier rare, snap it. 61.6% GIH with a huge +13.5 IWD and 2.5 ALSA — it wins games on its own as a BR villain threat, OH and drawn WR both above 61% so it's good early and late. First-pick caliber; trust the B+ grade and the even-better live numbers.
Provisional, grade-based read: niche UB villain rare. The 36.6% play rate and bare 53.5% GIH say it's frequently cut — a C- card that only earns its slot when your UB connive/villain synergies are deep. No guide enthusiasm, no big WR. Speculative pick for a committed UB deck; otherwise low priority.
The Serpent Society: Strong BG build-around, take it if you're in the lane. gih_wr null but gd_wr 55.5% and 3.6 ALSA back the LoL read and CGB B-: a deathtouch/ward body that, paired with instant-speed deathtouch like Widow's Bite, forces sacrifices and goes "absolutely savage." Provisional but high in dedicated BG; a weak signpost otherwise.
Speedball, New Warrior: Provisional role-player on grade — no guide notes, no WR splits beyond the basics. 52.2% GIH and slightly negative IWD (-2.0) on a C- UR legend is replacement-level; the shallow artifact pair gives it no home. Playable body if you're already UR, otherwise a low pick. Read is provisional.
Spider-Man, To the Rescue: Solid WG gold playable. A 55.2% OH versus 57.0% drawn WR and a strong 89.5% play rate point to a reliable role-player the GW heroes-matter deck wants. The slightly negative -0.7 IWD just means it's a body you'd rather have than topdeck. Good, low-effort pick in the format's #2 archetype; not a bomb.
Spider-Woman, Secret Agent: Strong, early pick. 60.3% GIH WR and a huge 92.3% play rate; the gap between 57.0% oh_wr and 62.4% gd_wr says she's a touch better drawn than opening but plays great either way. The WU teamwork gold signpost and a flexible flyer-tier body — high pick whenever you're in white-blue.
Storm, Windrider: Bomb — 63.0% GIH, +7.9 IWD, 2.5 ALSA make this far better than its C+ grade. A flying GW hero that breaks stalls and dominates this slow format; the absence of guide notes belies the data. One of the best things you can open in white-green; take it immediately.
The Super Hero Civil War: Format-defining bomb — first pick, not close. 70.2% GIH WR and a staggering +15.1 IWD are among the best numbers in the set; Numot calls it "absurd/disgusting, one of the best rares, not close." The awkwardness is real but irrelevant at this power level. Take it over almost anything.
Taskmaster, Mercenary Mimic: Good UB rare, take early in connive decks. 56.0% GIH, 70% play rate and 3.2 ALSA all point to a contested, above-rate body; the C grade undersells it — trust the WR. A flexible villain that slots into the best archetype in the format. Prioritize when you're UB.
Thanos, the Mad Titan: Provisional bomb (no WR yet) — lean on the C grade plus Numot's "highlight bomb" read: a splashable 4/4 deathtouch-lifelink with a board-wipe power-up, and red is the best splash. The colorless power-up cost is a real build constraint, so the floor is lower than a clean bomb. First-pick the ceiling, build toward it.
Thor Odinson: Good but fragile flyer, mid-pick. 53.5% GIH is more modest than "juiced Serra Angel" implies — flat IWD and a 61% play rate say it's a strong body that dies to the format's plentiful black removal and blue bounce, so it underdelivers relative to its stats. Still a stall-breaking flyer worth playing in RW; just not a bomb.
Titania, Rugged Rumbler: Solid aggressive playable. 56.0% GIH WR and +3.9 IWD beat the lukewarm guide reads — a 3-mana 5/5 ahead of curve is real tempo even with the discard tax and flimsy ward. The 80% play rate is earned. Good in BG, but its evaluation swings on your removal to back it up.
U.S.Agent, John Walker: Premium uncommon, take it high. 58.1% GIH, 87% play rate, 3.5 ALSA — an Orzhov 3/2 that auto-makes and auto-equips a +1/+2 shield with no tempo loss, flexible on mana value and great at punching through stalls. LoL's "great" matches the data; a clean WB goodstuff playable.
Vision Quest: Hidden gem — pick it high, well above its C+ grade. 63.8% GIH with a massive +9.6 IWD (one of the loudest signals in the set) and a strong 60.2% OH mean it's a near-bomb that swings games on its own, not just synergy. The data screams take it; the population's 64.4% play undersells it. Premium for UR.
War Machine, Legacy of Iron: Role-player for aggressive Boros. 53.0% GIH WR with -2.5 IWD (CGB C-) — fine but unexciting: a small evasive artifact hero that hands out a recurring +power buff, best when you've got bodies to swing with in RW. Mid-pick in its lane, replaceable elsewhere.
Winter Soldier, Icy Assassin: Strong WB rare, take it high. 60.6% GIH with +8.3 IWD and a 3.9 ALSA is well above its B- grade — the live data says this is closer to a bomb than a role-player. No notes, but the numbers carry it: an evasive value villain that anchors the attack-alone/WB deck. Trust the WR and prioritize.
Wolverine, Fierce Fighter: Near-bomb — first-pick RG. 63.0% GIH WR, +10.2 IWD, ALSA 2.2 and a B+ grade all line up: a sticky, evasive-or-recursive threat that dominates a slow board and is hard to race down. Take it highly whenever red-green is open; one of the best gold cards in your lane.
Worlds Within Worlds: Trap, do not play. No WR data, a 2.9% play rate and F grade tell you everything — this is unplayable in draft. A clunky GU sorcery with no real Limited home. Pass every time; it never makes the deck.
A.I.M. Synthoids: Solid common, an overperformer that beats its D+ grade — checks artifact, villain, and graveyard boxes while filling the format's 2-drop shortage. The 53.8% GIH is fine for a flexible early body with surveil; LLU's "people don't know the power" read holds. A good role-player, not a slam.
Arc Reactor: Unplayable — never maindeck. No WR data and an 18% play rate among the few who tried it; LLU flatly calls it a "Commander card." A 5-mana enters-tapped mana rock does nothing in this format. The F grade is accurate. Pass, even as a rare.
Captain America's Shield: Premium colorless rare — first-pickable, plays in any deck. The 1.6 ALSA and 58.1% GIH show the field already moved it up to "absurd": indestructible, +8/+0, taps a blocker, and on a flyer it's a recurring beater only exile answers. Trust the data over the split C-/C grades. Slam it.
Cosmic Cube: Take it high — the D grade is wrong; 59.5% GIH WR, +5.1 IWD, 1.4 ALSA and 96% play rate make this a genuine bomb-tier engine. The OH-null/62% drawn split says it snowballs once online. Needs big attackers (it free-casts spells up to your attacker's power), which any goodstuff deck has. Alex's B- is the right read.
Dependable Quinjet: Fixing filler, low priority. 54.6% GIH but a 37% play rate and crew 4 make it a clunky mana rock you take only to smooth a greedy multicolor soup, then cut once your fixing is solid. Fixing is less wanted here than usual. Late pick, situational.
H.E.R.B.I.E. Scout Unit: Solid colorless glue. 58.8% GIH WR and +2.4 IWD validate Mark's "goes in every deck" over Alex's 23rd-card read — a 4-mana cantripping 2/1 flyer that also ramps is a high-floor two-for-one in an air-stalled format. Slightly clogs the 4-slot, but take it; it fits any archetype.
Iron Man Armor: Near-format-staple equipment, take it high. 58.5% GIH, +5.3 IWD, and a 97.5% play rate / 1.3 ALSA mean nearly everyone plays it — auto-attaches for +2/+1 flying and animates into a flyer, so it breaks stalls and slots anywhere, not just artifact decks. LLU's B+ beats the C grade; trust the data and pick it early.
S.H.I.E.L.D. Helicarrier: Solid playable in WU, underrated by the community. 54.1% GIH with a low 29.1% play means most pass it, but Alex ran it over pushback and it carried as a 4/5 flyer that comes with two bodies — stall-breaking evasion plus big-dummy insurance. The Captain America self-crew combo is gravy. Holds Alex's C, not Mark's D+. Mid-pick, higher in blue-white.
Super-Adaptoid: Solid colorless glue, goes in any deck. 58.0% GIH WR with a great 1.9 ALSA and 92% play rate beat the CGB C / LLU C+ — a cheap legendary-count creature that scales with your legends and steals keywords, frictionless filler-plus that's especially good in this legend-dense set. Take it mid; never a dead pick.
The Ten Rings: Hard trap, never play it. No WR but a D- grade and unanimous LLU "F" — an 8-mana artifact that decks you too fast for a payoff that doesn't win. Picked occasionally (27.2% play) by people who got fooled by mythic shine. Pass every time.
Ultron, Artificial Malevolence: Strong but demanding mythic — a build-around, not a slam. The 55.4% GIH WR (no OH WR sample) reflects that it 'shines late, hard to fuel on curve' without an artifact density that rarely exists here. ALSA 1.6 is name-tax hype. C/C+ guides are fair; great payoff in a dedicated artifact deck, mediocre otherwise.
Ultron Drone: Filler, late pick for the right deck. The 54.1% GIH WR is buoyed by gd_wr; oh_wr is a weak 50.5% and play is only 38.4%, matching the D+ live read. It's a 2/3 artifact villain that power-ups into 4/5 + a 2/2 — a 'bingo space' for artifact/villain builds. Replaceable everywhere else.
Vibranium Energy Daggers: Filler/sideboard — 16.5% play rate and the D-/D grades tell the story. Equipment payoffs are too thin and equip-3 is too steep in a slow format; the 52.5% GIH comes from the few decks that found a use. Skip it; play real cards.
The Vision: Bomb — first-pickable colorless. 60.2% GIH WR, +5.2 IWD and a 1.3 ALSA (taken essentially first overall) with 98% play; it slots into any deck. A 2/5 flying/vigilance artifact with modal payoffs on noncreature casts — Alex would happily P1 it. The B- grade is low; trust the numbers and take it.
Viv Vision, Teen Synthezoid: Marginal colorless playable, not a high pick. The -0.2 IWD is the tell — drawing it doesn't help, confirming the D+ grades; a 3-mana 2/2 flyer whose card draw needs power 4+ that you rarely reach (too few cheap pumps). 54.4% GIH is replacement-level. A late flyer body, nothing more.
A.I.M. Labs: Strong utility land, prioritize for fixing/value — 56.3% GIH WR and +2.5 IWD on a colorless land that costs you nothing in deckbuilding is excellent. In a slow, splash-friendly format a free value/fixing land that goes in any deck is worth an early pick. Take it over marginal playables.
Asgardian Citadel: Solid utility land, easy include. 57.9% GIH and a strong 60.7% OH WR — a colorless land that earns its slot without costing you a spell, and fixing/utility lands are good in this format. Run it freely in most decks; high-floor, low-opportunity-cost pick.
Avengers Hangar: Premium fixing. A 60.6% GIH WR and 61.5% OH WR are excellent for a land — gain-life dual fixing with no real opportunity cost, exactly what a slow splash-friendly format wants. Beats its C grade; play as many as your colors need and prioritize over marginal spells.
Avengers Tower: Best of the utility lands — premium, near-free inclusion. 60.9% GIH and 84% play rate: in this hero-dense set you only need ~7-9 heroes for the instant-speed dig, and a land that draws a card is huge in grindy stalls. The D+ grade is badly wrong; guides agree it's great. Take it over marginal spells.
Baxter Building: Sneaky-good utility land — don't sleep on it. 58.2% GIH and 77.7% play vindicate the early-access revision (LR's F was wrong): it fixes any color AND is effectively "4, tap, draw a card" since 4-toughness creatures are everywhere, making it a real stall-breaker.
