Numot kept forgetting the draw mode and still won. Take it as low-opportunity-cost fixing.
Birnin Zana Plaza: Solid fixing land, take it for multicolor/splash decks. 57.1% GIH WR with oh_wr (59.6%) above gd_wr — you want it early to fix mana. No downside in a two-or-three color build (red is the best splash here); the CGB C undersells how smoothly mana enables the goodstuff plan. Grab one when you need fixing.
Castle Doom: Solid utility-land freeroll — better than its D- grade. 55.4% GIH with +4.0 IWD and a strong GD (59.2%) say it does real work; a colorless land that slots into any deck with upside. Mana/fixing is good in this format and this overperforms. Take it as a low-opportunity-cost land, especially in slower decks.
Dark Fortress: Solid value land, easy include. 53.1% GIH WR with +3.2 IWD and a 64% play rate for a colorless utility land that costs you almost nothing — exactly the kind of free edge this fixing-rich format rewards. C+ grade fits. Take it when the better cards are gone; near-zero opportunity cost in the right deck.
Fisk Tower: Playable utility land, take it for the fixing. 55.3% GIH WR and 56.6% play with a C grade — colorless lands are good in this well-fixed format and this slots into most decks. Not exciting, but a low-opportunity-cost include that smooths mana. Pick it up in the mid-to-late rounds.
Gathering Place: Solid utility land — a near-free include that smooths your deck, which is why it sees 67% play at a 4.0 ALSA. The 56.5% GIH is land-typical (note the -0.9 IWD, normal for a land). Good colorless pickup in the mid-rounds; the C+ grade is fair.
Gleaming Bastion: Premium utility land — take it early and run it in nearly any deck. 58.4% GIH WR and 3.9 ALSA for a colorless land is excellent; it's a near-free inclusion that smooths mana and adds late-game reach in a grindy format. Higher pick than its C+ grade suggests; the WR is the truth.
Hell's Kitchen: Fine utility land, low-opportunity-cost include. 54.2% GIH and +0.4 IWD are about what you'd expect from a colorless land — it smooths without costing a spell slot, hence the 61.5% play rate. Solid mana-fixing in a format that values it; take it when nothing better calls, never over a real card.
Hidden Lair: Excellent colorless land — 58.4% GIH WR, +4.9 IWD and a notable 62.1% OH WR mean it pulls weight even in your opener, rare for a utility land. Goes in every deck at no real cost. One of the best non-creature picks here; grab it.
Los Diablos Missile Base: Playable utility land. 55.0% GIH with a slightly negative IWD (-0.9), meaning it's fine in your opener but a weak topdeck. The colorless land earns near-free inclusion in decks that can use it. Take it mid-to-late; useful but not exciting.
Pym Technologies: Solid utility land. 56.6% GIH WR with a flat IWD says it's a free inclusion that fixes and adds reach without a slot cost. C grade is fair; grab it as painless mana that enables red splashes. Not a high pick but never a waste.
Stark Industries: Fine utility land, fringe playable. 56% GIH and a modest +1.9 IWD — it does a job (fixing/value) without warping picks, the C grade about right. A reasonable late inclusion when it fits, but nothing to prioritize; lower than Avengers Tower.
Subterranean Cavern: Fine fixing land, replaceable. 55.5% GIH at a 6.6 ALSA with a flat +0.6 IWD — it does its job smoothing mana but adds nothing else, which is why it wheels. The set's fixing is good and this is part of why. Grab it mid-late for two-color or splash decks; no rush.
Surveillance Room: Premium colorless utility land per Mark — first in every deck, second in most. 57.7% GIH WR and +2.5 IWD blow past the absurd CGB F and LR D: surveils on ETB, filters any color, and enables splashes (Killmonger, red) at near-zero cost. The fixing is too good in this format; pick it up cheaply and run it.
Training Compound: Good colorless utility land, take it. 55.3% GIH, positive C+ grade backed by a 65.1% play rate — drafters keep it and it performs. Near-zero deck-building cost in a format where fixing and mana sinks are valuable. A reliable inclusion; pick it over marginal playables.
Villainous Hideout: Good value land for villain decks, mid pick. The 57.2% GIH WR and +5.2 IWD overshoot its D+ grade — a colorless fixing land that connives off a villain each turn is a real card-selection engine in BR/heavy-villain builds. Least of the three uncommon lands but still solid. Take it if your villain count supports it.
Archangel of Thune: No data, but a known premium mythic — grade-based read, treat as a bomb. A lifegain-into-permanent-pump engine that snowballs the board fast and flies, breaking stalls in a format with essentially no wipes. If it's in the pool at this rarity, first-pick it; provisional only because no live WR exists.
Concerted Effort: No live data, so this read is provisional. As a white go-wide enchantment that shares keywords across your team, it leans into GW heroes and the format's safe go-wide plans (board wipes are essentially nonexistent here). Likely a build-around mythic — speculative high pick only if you're already wide; otherwise a flexible later grab.
Don't Move: No data and no guide notes — provisional read only. As a white mythic sorcery it's likely a removal/tempo effect worth respecting on rarity, but with null WR and null grade this is a take-on-faith-and-see card. Default to picking white mythics over commons until live numbers contradict.
Ephemerate: No data and no grade — provisional read only. As a reprint, this is a one-mana blink with rebound: premium when you have ETB heroes (Falcon, Hero in Training, Coulson) to double, mediocre filler without. In a slow GW heroes/ETB-value deck it's a strong pick; evaluate against your blink targets. Bomb-adjacent in the right shell.
Final Showdown: No data — provisional read only. A white mythic instant with no WR, grade, or ALSA recorded; likely a rarely-drafted bomb-or-niche effect. White is the #2 color and the home of premium answers, so treat an unknown white mythic instant as worth a speculative early look, but verify the actual card before committing.
Light of Promise: No live data — read is provisional. As a white mythic aura, the archetype-defining concern is the classic aura two-for-one risk (they kill the creature, you lose both), but white is the #2 color and bombs here are punishing. Grade-based unknown; evaluate the actual text at the table and lean playable given the color, but cautiously.
Path to Exile: Provisional but unmistakable: premium removal. No MSH data, but Path is best-in-class one-mana exile, and removal is scarce and at a premium in this slow format. Treat it as a top-tier pick — the land downside barely matters when stalls form. Slam it.
Return to the Ranks: No live data yet, so this is a provisional read — no CGB grade either. White mass-reanimation/recursion mythics are typically slow build-arounds that overperform in go-wide hero shells (safe here with no board wipes) but can rot in hand. Treat as a speculative midrange payoff; play if your GW heroes deck is creature-dense, otherwise risky.
Righteous Fury: No live data — provisional read on a white mythic sorcery. With no GIH, ALSA, grade, or guide notes, treat it as a speculative high pick on rarity and color alone (white is the #2 color and home to punishing bombs). Default to taking it early and trusting white's track record until data says otherwise.
Steelshaper's Gift: Provisional, grade-based only — no WR or CGB data and no guide notes. As an equipment tutor it's purely a build-around enabler that needs a strong Sword (e.g., Sword of Fire and Ice) or aggressive aura/equipment package to justify a card slot; in a goodstuff format that payoff is rarely there. Treat as a low pick unless your deck is equipment-centric.
Teferi's Protection: No data and no grade — provisional. This is a powerful protective instant by reputation (fog-your-turn, phase out your board), but with null WR and no guide notes the read is unanchored. In a sweeperless slow format its blowout potential is lower than in Constructed; treat as a niche, splashy white pick until data exists.
Counterspell: No live data, so read provisionally — but it's a known quantity: hard, unconditional UU counter at instant speed. In a slow, two-for-one-hungry format where removal is premium and many threats are synergy linchpins, answering anything for two mana is excellent. Treat as a high pick / premium interaction in any blue deck.
Cyberdrive Awakener: No data; provisional grade-based read leans high. A blue artifact mythic that animates and pumps your artifacts/equipment — strong in an artifacts-matter build but the set's UR artifacts archetype is the shallowest, so it's deck-dependent. Take it as a speculative bomb if you're in blue artifacts; otherwise a strong-but-narrow pick.
Dig Through Time: No data yet, grade-based read. Delve card-draw is a known strong effect, and in a slow grindy format where card advantage is scarce, a cheap dig-for-two is excellent. Provisionally a premium blue pick — exactly the kind of two-for-one engine this set rewards. Take it highly until data says otherwise.
Harbinger of the Seas: No WR yet — provisional, grade-blind read. A blue mythic creature with a 5.8 ALSA, meaning the field is letting it wheel surprisingly late, which hints at a build-around or underwhelming body rather than a slam. Take it speculatively for UB/UR, but the late ALSA says temper expectations until data lands.
Lord of Atlantis: No WR data; mythic, 4.6 ALSA suggests it's taken reasonably high. As a reprint it's a Merfolk lord — a narrow tribal anthem with essentially no Merfolk support in this set, so it reads as a 2/2 islandwalk body that mostly does nothing here. Provisional: low-impact unless the set has hidden Merfolk; likely a trap. Don't prioritize.
Mechanized Production: No data — provisional skip. A blue mythic Aura with nothing recorded; auras that buy you a build-around payoff are usually low-floor in this removal-light-but-grindy format, and the UR artifact theme is the shallowest. Treat as a build-around gamble, not a default pick, until you confirm the text.
Narset's Reversal: No live data — provisional. A blue mythic instant; in a slow, removal-light format a copy-and-bounce-spell answer skews narrow and reactive, better against bombs than as a maindeck staple. Likely a strong but situational include given blue is the #1 color. Grade-based read; confirm the text and lean role-player.
Reconnaissance Mission: Provisional, grade-based read; the caption is mangled but LLU's B- and the likely flash-flying-vehicle-that-flickers profile point to a strong tempo-and-value play — flyers break stalls and flicker abuses ETBs. Treat as a high pick pending data, leaning on the B- review.
Show and Tell: No data and no grade — provisional. Symmetric cheat-into-play effects are notoriously double-edged in Limited: you help the opponent unless you have the bigger bomb, and in this slow format the symmetry usually backfires. Treat as a trap unless you're built around slamming a specific haymaker; default to leaving it in the board.
Simulacrum Synthesizer: No data, provisional. A blue mythic artifact with no WR, grade, or notes — read is rarity-and-color only. Blue is the format's best color, so it's worth a speculative early pick, but artifact payoffs (UR) are the shallowest archetype, so temper expectations. Take it on spec and learn it in play.
Three Steps Ahead: Provisional, grade-based only — no data or notes yet. A blue mythic instant in the de-facto best UB tempo/connive lane is exactly where premium tricks shine; the flexible-counterspell/protection class of card historically over-performs in slow blue decks. Speculative high pick pending live numbers.
Dauthi Voidwalker: No data, no grade — provisional, but pedigree screams premium. An evasive, hard-to-block black body with built-in graveyard hate and a steal mode is a known bomb elsewhere; in a slow grindy format the unblockable clock plus disruption should overperform. Lean take-it-high on reputation until WR confirms.
Deadly Dispute: No data yet; provisional read. A 1B instant sac-for-two-cards-and-a-treasure is premium card advantage and fixing — and card advantage is scarce in this format, so it overperforms its humble look. Wants fodder (tokens, dying villains) to feel free. Strong playable, prioritize in black sacrifice/villain decks; grade-based call.
Extinction Event: No WR data, but a black sorcery board wipe in a format with essentially NONE — read it as premium-to-bomb. Sweepers are uniquely valuable here against go-wide and sticky threats. Provisional since there's no live data, but if it cleans the board it's a high pick for any black deck.
Final Act: No live data, provisional read. A black mythic sorcery, almost certainly removal or a finisher — and removal is at a premium in this slow format. Treat as a likely high pick on rarity and color alone; black's villain/removal suite is deep, so expect this to be a real card. Grab it and confirm in play.
Massacre Girl: No data, no notes — but the name carries weight. Historically Massacre Girl is a one-card board sweep, and this format has essentially NO board wipes, so a real mythic version would be a premium answer to go-wide. Read is provisional on null stats; if it does anything like its namesake, first-pick it.
No Mercy: No data, mythic black enchantment — provisional. As a reprint, No Mercy is a passive removal engine that kills anything dealing combat damage to you, brutal in a slow, grindy stall-format where it dominates the ground. Reads as a premium defensive bomb in BX control; high pick on text alone, pending data.
Chaos Warp: No data — provisional, but lean playable. A red mythic instant; in a removal-scarce format any catch-all red answer earns its slot, and red is the best splash. Grade-blind here, so confirm the effect, but a flexible red removal-style instant is the kind of card to value highly in this slow set.
Fiery Emancipation: No live data — provisional, likely a trap in Limited. A high-cost red triple-damage enchantment does nothing the turn it lands and the format has no wipes to reset around it; without an immediate board impact it reads as a win-more build-around. Grade-based read; expect a low pick unless your aggressive RW deck can abuse it.
Fury of the Horde: No data and no guide note, so this is a provisional grade-less read. As a red mythic sorcery in a slow, non-racy format, a one-shot burst/extra-combat effect is suspect unless it's reach or removal — lean cautious until WR appears. Speculative mid-pick at most.
Monstrous Rage: No live WR or grade, so grade-based provisional. As a cheap red combat trick/pump it slots into the RW spells-and-tricks deck — the format's most aggressive lane — where tricks two-for-one in combat. Cheap interaction is welcome; a fine role-player for prowess/aggro builds, not a premium pick.
Seize the Day: No live data — provisional. A red mythic sorcery with nothing to anchor on but rarity. Red is the format's best splash, so a mythic spell is a reasonable speculative early grab; lean on it being an extra-turn or burst effect given the name. Pick on spec until WR data lands.
Bedlam: Provisional, grade-based only — no WR, CGB, or notes. A red mythic enchantment is hard to slot into this slow, stall-prone format unless it generates repeatable removal or pressure; red here is a splash, not a base. Read is a cautious mid pick until data lands — confirm the effect before committing.
Beast Within: Provisional but clearly premium removal — no WR/grade, but this answers ANYTHING (creature, bomb, even a land) at instant speed for the cost of a 3/3 token. In a format where removal is high-quality, low-quantity, and at a premium, unconditional catch-all answers are gold. Take it high in any green deck.
Defense of the Heart: No live data — grade-based and provisional. Historically a powerful enchantment that fetches your two biggest creatures for free once an opponent has three, but it's slow, telegraphed, and does nothing the turn it lands in a format with little ramp payoff. Speculative build-around at best; don't bank on it without a deep top-end.
Force of Vigor: No data; provisional. A green free instant that blows up artifacts/enchantments — premium sideboard tech against this set's artifact and Plan decks, marginal as a maindeck card. Board card more than a maindeck slam; grade-based read says situational. Value it as flexible best-of-three answer, low main-pick priority.
Heroic Intervention: No WR data but a telling 3.9 ALSA means people pick it earlier than a typical filler. A cheap green protection instant (hexproof + indestructible) is a clean blowout against this format's premium spot removal, defending your synergy legends. Provisionally a solid reactive playable; better in the abstract than most green commons.
Primal Vigor: No WR or notes — provisional. A green mythic enchantment; the namesake doubles tokens/counters, which would supercharge GW go-wide and GU counters, but symmetric token-doublers are clunky and often overrated in Limited. Speculative pick for a dedicated counters/tokens build only; don't reach without seeing it perform.
Rancor: No data, mythic green Aura — provisional but strong. The reprint is a recurring +2/+0 trample that returns to hand when the creature dies, generating relentless value and aggression — exactly the sticky single-threat enabler this wipe-light format rewards. A high green pick on reputation; evaluate as premium aggressive/synergy glue.
Steely Resolve: No data — provisional skip. A green mythic enchantment with nothing recorded; protection/hexproof-style enchantments tend to be narrow build-arounds that two-for-one you against removal. Treat as a sideboard/combo piece pending the actual text rather than a maindeck pick.
Unnatural Growth: No live data — provisional. A green mythic doubling enchantment that buffs your team in combat — splashy but, like most no-immediate-impact enchantments, slow in a format where it does nothing on cast. Grade-based read; potentially strong in a go-wide green board but more win-more than bomb. Confirm at the table.
Anthem of Champions: Provisional; no WR or grade. A WG anthem enchantment slots straight into the strong, low-effort GW heroes/go-wide deck, and with essentially no board wipes in MSH, sticky team pumps are unusually safe. Promising on archetype fit — take it if you're in white-green, grade-pending.
Aurelia, the Warleader: No data yet, but this is a known bomb-tier angel — provisional but confident. An extra-combat flyer that breaks stalls (exactly what this slow format rewards) and closes games fast. In a WR spells shell she's a haymaker; treat as a first-pick-caliber finisher pending live numbers.
Black Panther, Wakandan King: No data yet, but read it as a likely bomb on spec. A WG mythic legend sits squarely in the strong, low-effort GW Heroes-matter pair (archetype #2), so the color identity and rarity point to a high pick. Grade-free read: take it early and trust the gold-mythic-in-a-good-pair profile.
Captain America, First Avenger: Provisional, grade-based only — no data yet, but a WUR mythic legend in this rare-defined set is almost certainly a build-defining bomb where the colors line up. Three-color cost means you need fixing (Surveillance Room helps), but power lives in the legends — take it as a likely first-pick and let it steer your deck.
Escape to the Wilds: Provisional, grade-based read absent — but as a Gruul card-advantage engine it's strong. Drawing two and ramping/playing off the top is exactly the two-for-one this card-scarce format rewards, and RG power-up wants the gas. No data yet, but lean high pick in RG; reputation is excellent.
Fight to the Death: No data; provisional. A WR instant that mass-fights creatures is splashy pseudo-removal — potentially a blowout two-for-one in the go-wide-safe MSH board states, but symmetric and board-dependent, so it's a finisher for aggressive RW spells decks rather than clean spot removal. Promising but situational; grade-based read.
Iron Man, Titan of Innovation: No data, but a mythic legend — treat as a bomb provisionally. A UR artifact creature that should dominate the board and reward an artifacts build. The UR artifacts archetype is the set's shallowest, so it's best as a powerful standalone threat rather than a synergy linchpin. First-pickable on rate; read is grade-based.
Privileged Position: No data, provisional grade-based read. A GW enchantment that blanks targeted removal is strong insurance in a format defined by premium spot removal aimed at synergy legends. Likely a build-around mythic for go-wide GW heroes; speculative high pick if you're in those colors, otherwise a flexible grab. Confirm in play.
Ravenous Tyrannosaurus: No data, grade-blind read. An RG mythic dinosaur — almost certainly a big beater, and the "big dummy" rule applies: a no-ETB fatty is a trap that gets raced unless it has reach, trample, or an enrage/eat payoff. RG power-up/ramp wants a finisher, so it may fit there. Provisional; verify before prioritizing.
Storm, Force of Nature: No data, three-color mythic — provisional and build-restricted. A URG legend is only castable in a heavy Temur/wedge build, so for most drafts it's uncastable upside. If your fixing supports it she's presumably a bomb, but the color cost makes it a gamble; treat as a speculative pick that demands you commit to the wedge, not a safe early grab.
Sundering Growth: No data — provisional role-player. A GW mythic instant; GW heroes-matter is a strong, low-effort archetype, and a flexible instant there could be a fine value/utility card. Grade-blind, so confirm the effect, but if it's removal or a two-for-one it slots cleanly into the format's #2 archetype.
Warleader's Call: No live data — provisional. A WR anthem-plus-pinger enchantment is exactly the go-wide, stall-proof effect this no-wipes format rewards, echoing the strong Avengers Assemble! profile in the same archetype. Grade-based read, but lean high pick for RW/go-wide; this is the kind of safe, sticky payoff the format punishes opponents with.
Wolverine, Best There Is: Provisional, no data — but a marquee RG mythic legend in a rare-defined set where power lives in the legends. Expect a build-around bomb worth a high pick on reputation; RG power-up wants resilient threats and red is the best splash. Take early and confirm once WR lands.
Horn of Greed: No data and no grade — provisional, and symmetric card-draw is a trap-shaped read here. It draws your opponent cards too, and in a grindy format that often helps them more than you unless you're the one landing more lands. Speculative at best; default to leaving it unless you're aggressively going wide and ahead on board.
Roaming Throne: No live data — provisional, but pedigree-strong. A colorless mythic artifact creature plays in any deck, and Roaming Throne is a known powerful doubler; treat it as a speculative early pick on universal castability alone. Take it high and let it slot into whatever you draft.
Sword of Fire and Ice: Provisional, grade-based only — no MSH data, but this is one of the strongest equipment ever printed: +2/+2, pro red/blue, ping-2-and-draw on hit turns any creature into a removal-proof two-for-one engine. In a slow grindy format with scarce card advantage, that's a colorless first-pick bomb. Slam it, fix to wield it.
